trust_decision.summary: The API access-log middleware takes the username from the unauthenticated Basic-auth header (or the JWT sub) and writes it straight into the plain-text API log line. The only decision is whether the request data is safe to write as a log line, and it is made nowhere before custom_logging formats it.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the Basic-auth username, and this is the only line that decodes it from the Authorization header before logging.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any wazuh-apid HTTP request carrying an Authorization: Basic (or Bearer) header, e.g. POST /security/user/authenticate; access_log is called for every request by the access-log middleware (api/api/middlewares.py:265-266)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the username, so a solver can argue that the request path is just a URL the client chose, outside the 'unsanitized username' report, and that the plain sink at api/api/alogging.py:255 is a generic formatter rather than the reported field.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same user value goes into the structured JSON log (api/api/alogging.py:244), which already escapes it, and into the plain log. Legitimate usernames and percent-encoded path parameters (agent, group or file names) must still be logged readably. An over-broad fix that rejects the request (4xx) or strips characters would change authentication results or lose audit information. Escaping without escaping backslash leaves 'user\\n' ambiguous with an escaped newline.

O6_input_shapes: JWT sub containing control characters (test only; sub is a server-signed user id)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Request path from scope['path'] goes unescaped into the same plain log line; the ASGI server percent-decodes it, so %0d%0a in the URL becomes a raw CRLF
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the Basic-auth username; the path is a different field and 'just the URL', and any 404 path is still logged
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fix site, emitted at api/api/alogging.py:255-257 (one file away)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The warning added by the fix logs Path: {path} raw (it uses user!r only for the username), so the new log line is itself a route for the same injection
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a diagnostic warning written by the fix itself, and the username in it is already repr-escaped

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Escape at the formatter (custom_logging) rather than the caller, so every field sharing the plain line (user, path, hash_auth_context) is covered; a planted hash_auth_context taken from an unsigned source would be a realistic sibling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: custom_logging is the shared plain-text sink, and hash_auth_context already crosses from token claims (api/api/middlewares.py:100-101)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The login-block warning could realistically include the attempted username next to the host
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers commonly add the attempted user to brute-force warnings for auditing

O9_family: CWE-117 log injection (CRLF into plain-text API access log)

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 + pytest (pytest-asyncio, freezegun), connexion 3/starlette, uvicorn; the framework package is on the path

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace \n/\r/\t in the Basic-auth username inside access_log only, leaving the path and the shared custom_logging format string unescaped.

out_of_scope_notes: DAPI debug log of the forwarded request at framework/wazuh/core/cluster/dapi/dapi.py:672 formats bytes with repr, so it is escaped; not pursued.
The fix commit title says 'validate user name in framework', but the diff changes only the API middleware.
